newsitem.title: GERMANY: German computer maker takes stake in Escom France.
newsitem.headline: German computer maker takes stake in Escom France.

text.p: German computer maker ComTech, which last month took over bankrupt Escom AG's network of 90 stores in Germany, said on Wednesday it had acquired a 65 percent stake in Escom's French subsidiary.

The French Escom division has some 130 retail outlets at leading French merchants such as Casino, Leclerc, Surcoufe and International Computer. It had been acquired previously in a management buy-out.
But it would have been difficult for the new owners to carry under the Escom name because ComTech had already acquired the national and international rights to the Escom brand name.
Escom declared bankruptcy in early August after failing to win the support of creditors for fresh cash after international expansion and depreciation of stocks forced it into insolvency.

ComTech is a personal computer maker based in Waiblingen near Stuttgart in southern Germany. After the takeover of the Escom stores, it became Germany's second-largest computer retailer with 195 stores.
The acquisition of a majority stake in the French Escom division marks the first steps outside of Germany for ComTech.
